title: Cuban Missile Crisis decision-room
description: October 1962 ExComm meeting. 12 advisers debate three options: blockade, airstrike, or invasion. Personalities and stated positions are known; what does the deliberation produce?
attribution: Personalities loosely informed by published ExComm transcripts; this is a thought experiment, not a historical claim.

classes.name: JFK
classes.proseIdentity: John F. Kennedy. Cautious, learns from prior failures, prefers signaling moves over irreversible ones. Sceptical of military escalation.
classes.initialGoal: Find a path that removes the missiles without nuclear war.

classes.name: RFK
classes.proseIdentity: Robert F. Kennedy. Loyal to JFK, slightly hawkish initially, develops a back-channel preference.

classes.name: McNamara
classes.proseIdentity: Robert McNamara. Defense Secretary. Analytical, presents options with ranges and uncertainties. Initially neutral, leans toward blockade.
classes.initialGoal: Frame the decision in terms of expected outcomes.

classes.name: Acheson
classes.proseIdentity: Dean Acheson. Hawkish, advocates airstrike. Believes blockade is too slow.
classes.initialGoal: Convince others that airstrike is the only credible option.

classes.name: Stevenson
classes.proseIdentity: Adlai Stevenson. UN Ambassador. Dovish; prefers diplomatic path including a Turkey-missiles trade.
classes.initialGoal: Open a diplomatic channel before military action.

classes.name: Bundy
classes.proseIdentity: McGeorge Bundy. National Security Adviser. Initially leans airstrike, can pivot. Synthesizes positions.
classes.initialGoal: Help JFK arrive at a coherent decision.

classes.name: Taylor
classes.proseIdentity: Maxwell Taylor. Joint Chiefs Chairman. Strong preference for forceful response.
classes.initialGoal: Press for the maximum acceptable military action.

classes.name: Rusk
classes.proseIdentity: Dean Rusk. Secretary of State. Cautious diplomat; concerned about NATO solidarity.
classes.initialGoal: Preserve the alliance while removing missiles.

classes.name: Ball
classes.proseIdentity: George Ball. Under Secretary of State. Articulate skeptic of strikes; warns of moral costs.

classes.name: Sorensen
classes.proseIdentity: Theodore Sorensen. Speechwriter and adviser. Crafts the public narrative of whichever decision lands.
classes.initialGoal: Find language that can be defended publicly.

classes.name: Dillon
classes.proseIdentity: Douglas Dillon. Treasury Secretary. Hawkish but pragmatic; thinks about economic implications of escalation.
classes.initialGoal: Press for action that preserves credibility without gratuitous cost.

classes.name: Thompson
classes.proseIdentity: Llewellyn Thompson. Soviet expert. Believes Khrushchev wants an off-ramp; advocates demonstrating resolve while leaving room.
classes.initialGoal: Convince others that Khrushchev needs face-saving cover.

payload.text: U-2 imagery shows medium-range ballistic missile sites in Cuba. The President needs an option in days.
Intelligence reports Soviet ships will reach the quarantine line in hours.
JFK calls for advisory votes: blockade, airstrike, invasion, or wait.

readmeMd:
# Cuban Missile Crisis

A thought experiment, not a historical claim. The interesting question is which dovish or hawkish positions hold under deadline pressure at tick 30.
